case.title: Mr. Timothy Ikujuni v. Registered Trustees of Ikoyi Club 1938

procedural_history.originating_proceedings: Claimant filed suit NICN/LA/433/2012 against the defendant. Judgment was delivered on 21st March, 2014 in favour of the claimant.
procedural_history.procedural_posture: Ruling on motion for stay of execution of judgment pending appeal.

previous_decisions.decision: Judgment delivered in favour of the claimant.

interlocutory_applications.application: Motion for stay of execution of judgment pending appeal

appeals.appeal: Appeal filed against the judgment of 21st March, 2014

material_facts: Judgment was delivered in favour of the claimant on 21st March, 2014.
The defendant filed an appeal against the judgment.
The defendant filed a motion for stay of execution pending appeal.

chronology.event: Judgment delivered in favour of claimant.
Defendant filed motion for stay of execution.
Ruling delivered granting conditional stay of execution.

reliefs_sought.relief: An order staying execution of the judgment of this court delivered on 21st March, 2014 pending the hearing and determination of the Appeal filed against the said judgment.

issues_for_determination.issue: Whether this court should grant a stay of execution in the circumstance of this case.

defendant_arguments: The court has power to grant stay of execution under Section 47 of the National Industrial Court Act, 2006.
The grant of stay is discretionary.

Applicant must show: competent and valid appeal, appeal raises unanswerable question of law, special or exceptional circumstance, inability of respondent to refund judgment sum, and balance of convenience in favour of defendant.
Grounds of appeal are unanswerable in favour of applicant.
If execution is not stayed, it would be impossible for claimant to refund the judgment sum.
Preservation of res prevents judgment on appeal from being rendered nugatory.
Balance of convenience is on the applicant.
respondent_arguments: Principles for stay of execution are laid down in cases.
Courts have discretion to grant or refuse stay, considering competing rights.
Winning party has right to fruits of judgment.
Applicant must show special and exceptional circumstances.
Facts in affidavit do not support special circumstance.
Res is only a monetary claim; allowing defendant to retain judgment debt gives undue advantage.
Applicant's affidavit falls short of legal requirements.
Grounds of appeal are frivolous and raise no substantial or recondite point of law.
Defendant participated in proceedings and did not protest denial of fair hearing.
Appeal based on Section 243(3) of the Constitution requires leave of the Court of Appeal.
Balance of convenience is not in defendant's favour.

findings_of_law.finding: The court has discretion under Section 47 of the National Industrial Court Act, 2006 to grant stay of execution either unconditionally or upon conditions.
A stay of execution will only be granted if there are special or exceptional circumstances.
Arguable grounds of appeal alone do not constitute special circumstances for granting stay.

judicial_analysis.reasoning: The court considered the competing interests of the parties and the guiding principles from appellate courts. It found that a conditional stay would meet the justice of the case, ensuring that the judgment sum is preserved in an interest-yielding account pending appeal.

issue_analysis.issue: Whether this court should grant a stay of execution in the circumstance of this case.

arguments.claimant: Opposed the application, arguing that the applicant failed to show special circumstances, that the grounds of appeal are frivolous, and that the balance of convenience is not in favour of the applicant.
arguments.defendant: Argued that the court has discretion to grant stay, that the appeal raises unanswerable questions of law, that the applicant would suffer irreparable loss if stay is not granted, and that the balance of convenience is in its favour.

issue_analysis.judicial_analysis: The court reviewed the principles for granting stay of execution, including the need for special or exceptional circumstances. It noted that the court has discretion under Section 47 of the NIC Act to grant a conditional stay. The court compared the competing interests and found that a conditional stay would be appropriate to preserve the res pending appeal.
issue_analysis.holding: The court granted a conditional stay of execution, ordering the defendant to deposit the judgment sum in an interest-yielding account.
issue_analysis.ratio_decidendi: A conditional stay of execution may be granted where it would meet the justice of the case, such as by preserving the judgment sum in an interest-yielding account pending appeal.

holdings.issue: Whether this court should grant a stay of execution in the circumstance of this case.
holdings.result: Defendant ordered to deposit judgment sum in interest-yielding account within 30 days.

ratio_decidendi.principle: A conditional stay of execution may be granted where it would meet the justice of the case, such as by preserving the judgment sum in an interest-yielding account pending appeal.
ratio_decidendi.application: The court applied this principle by ordering the defendant to deposit the judgment sum in an interest-yielding account.
